newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia waits to see if can resume Russia flights.
newsitem.headline: Latvia waits to see if can resume Russia flights.

text.p: Latvian airline Air Baltic, in which Scandinavian Airlines has a large stake, is waiting to see if it can start flying between Russia and Latvia, Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans said on Monday.
Russia has refused to allow Air Baltic to fly between Riga, Moscow and St Petersburg after its predecessor, Latavio, ran up debts of $2.8 million for landing rights and service fees in Moscow.
Latvia has now decided its privatisation agency will repay Latavio's debts and the agency now has to reach a settlement with the creditors.
"That will take at least a month," Krishtopans told a news conference.
The privatisation agency was chosen to repay the debt as it controls the 51 percent the Latvian government owns in Latavio, which no longer operates flights and will soon cease to exist.
Krishtopans said it was then up to the Russian side to decide whether to allow Air Baltic to fly to Russia.
A lack of flights to Russia was one of the reasons Air Baltic made a bigger-than-expected loss after in first year.
Flights to Russia are currently carried out by Russian Aeroflot and Transaero and only one Latvian company, Riair, flies to Russia.
